release_notes.title: Refund Colors, Bank-Statement In/Out Formatting & Messy-File Import Detection
release_notes.summary: Amount colors now reflect real money movement, not just a Revenue/Expense label: credit card and expense-report refunds show as a positive green amount, and bank-statement withdrawals show red in parentheses while deposits show green. CSV/Excel import also now detects messy files — leading account-info rows before the real header, and trailing totals/footer rows — and lets you confirm or fix both before importing.

changes.text: Credit card and expense-report refunds/returns/credits now display as a positive amount in green, instead of a negative red parenthesized number, on All Transactions, Revenue, Expenses, and the Add Transaction recent-entries list. The underlying P&L math is unchanged — refunds still correctly reduce the expense total.

Bank statement amounts follow standard ledger convention: money in (deposits) shows green; money out (withdrawals) shows red and in parentheses, e.g. "($1,800.00)". This coloring is now applied consistently to every expense/revenue amount app-wide, not just newly-imported bank data.

Expense Report CSV imports now detect refund/credit/return rows (via a Type column, or the file's own negative sign) and store them as a credit that reduces the expense total, matching how Credit Card imports already worked.

CSV/Excel import now shows the top 7 raw rows of your file and lets you pick which row is actually your column headers — useful for bank/card exports that lead with a couple of "Account: ..." or "Statement Period: ..." lines before the real header row. The likely header row is auto-detected and highlighted; override it with one dropdown if it's wrong.

Trailing totals/footer rows (e.g. a "Total,,,$1,234.56" row at the end of the file) are auto-detected and excluded from the import by default, with a one-click toggle to include them if the detection is wrong.
Both detections are quiet on well-formed files — if your file already starts with a proper header row and has no footer row, nothing changes and no extra prompts appear.

release_notes.title: Track Where Your Data Comes From — Source / Account Tracking
release_notes.summary: Every transaction can now be tagged with where it came from — a bank, a credit card, a sales channel, or a manual account name. CSV imports of a Bank Statement or Credit Card Statement now ask which bank/card it is; manual entries get a free-text Source / Account field. A new Source column appears on All Transactions, Revenue, and Expenses, and Reports can break Revenue/Expense down by Source instead of Category.

changes.text: CSV import now asks for the account name for Bank Statement and Credit Card Statement imports ("Which bank is this?" / "Which card/bank is this?") and applies it to every row in the file. Sales, Expense Report, and "map a Type column myself" imports get the same field as an optional Source name.
A CSV can also be mapped directly to a Source/Account column if different rows come from different accounts — the per-row value overrides the file-level name.
The account name you type is remembered per import type, so re-importing next month's statement pre-fills it.
Manual entry (Add Transaction) now has a Source / Account field with autocomplete from previously used accounts, for tracking things like "Chase Checking", "Cash", or "PayPal".

A Source column is now shown — and inline-editable — on All Transactions, Revenue, and Expenses, including the mobile edit sheet. All Transactions gained a Source filter dropdown, and the search box on every table now matches Source too.
Reports → Expense Breakdown and Revenue Breakdown got a Group By toggle: switch between Category and Source / Account to see revenue or spend broken down by where it came from.
CSV/Excel export and File Sync now include the Source column, so it round-trips on export and re-import.

release_notes.title: CSV Import: Data-Type-Aware Revenue/Expense Classification
release_notes.summary: Fixes credit card transactions being misclassified as revenue on import. A new "What kind of data is this?" step lets you tell the importer whether a file is Sales/Revenue, a Credit Card Statement, an Expense Report, or a Bank Statement — each uses the correct accounting convention. Unmapped transactions are also auto-categorized using industry-standard expense categories based on the merchant name.

changes.text: Credit card statements no longer import as Revenue. Previously, files with no Type column (or an issuer-provided Type column like "Sale") fell back to a plain amount-sign guess or a keyword match that treated "Sale" as revenue — correct for a sales ledger, wrong for a credit card charge.

New "What kind of data is this?" selector in the Import CSV mapping screen: Sales/Revenue data, Credit Card Statement, Expense Report, Bank Statement, or the original "I'll map a Type column myself." Each applies the right revenue/expense rule automatically, and the Type column mapping becomes optional once you pick one.

Credit card imports understand issuer Type labels (Sale/Purchase/Fee → Expense, Payment → skipped as a transfer, Return/Refund/Credit → a negative expense that reduces your total) and, when no Type column exists, a configurable amount-sign convention (positive = charge, as on most cards, or negative = charge, as on Chase).
Bank statement imports let you specify whether positive amounts are deposits (Revenue) or withdrawals (Expense).

Industry-standard merchant categorization: rows with no mapped category are auto-categorized from the description — e.g. Uber/DoorDash → Travel & Meals, Shell/Chevron → Vehicle & Fuel, AWS/Zoom/Slack → Software & Subscriptions, Staples/Amazon → Office Supplies, using the same category set as the rest of the app. Newly-used categories are added to your category list automatically.
The chosen import source is remembered for next time, since re-importing the same kind of file (e.g. a monthly card statement) is common.
The original "I'll map a Type column myself" mode is unchanged — existing imports that rely on it behave exactly as before.

release_notes.title: Reports Tab, PDF Export & Configurable Auto Sign-Out
release_notes.summary: New Reports tab with a proper Profit & Loss statement, a line-by-line Year-over-Year comparison, and four analysis reports — printable and exportable to letter-size PDF or CSV. Plus: refreshing the page no longer signs you out (configurable inactivity timer, default 5 min) and a always-visible Sign Out button.

changes.text: P&L Statement: industry-standard common-size income statement — Revenue, COGS, Gross Profit, Operating Expenses and Net Profit, each shown as a dollar amount and as a % of revenue, with KPI summary cards on top.

P&L Year-over-Year: compares any year against the prior year line by line, with dollar change, % change and up/down arrows, plus a grouped bar chart of Revenue, Gross Profit, Op. Expenses and Net Profit.
Time-frame selector: This Year, Last Year, Year to Date, This/Last Quarter, This/Last Month, All Time, or a custom From/To date range — resolved consistently across every report.
Four analysis reports: Expense Breakdown and Revenue Breakdown (doughnut + ranked table with % of total), Monthly Trend (revenue/expense/net line chart), and Quarterly Summary (Q1–Q4 P&L).
Industry-aware suggestions: the Reports tab recommends the most useful next reports based on your selected industry template and whether you track COGS.

Save as PDF and Print: every report opens a print-friendly US Letter (8.5 x 11 in) statement — use Print, or Save PDF to save one via the browser's built-in PDF export. CSV export (formula-injection sanitized) is also available. Jump to Reports with g then p.
Refreshing the page no longer signs you out. You stay signed in and are only asked to re-enter your PIN (or sign in again) after a period of inactivity.
Configurable auto sign-out timer in Settings → Security & Session: choose 1, 5, 15, 30, 60 minutes or Never. Default is 5 minutes. Reduces reliance on the auth server on every refresh.
Always-visible Sign Out button in the sidebar (desktop) and the More menu (mobile).

release_notes.title: Industry Templates, Smart Categories, Keyboard Shortcuts & Bulk Actions
release_notes.summary: 6 polish features: one-click industry setup (Consulting/E-commerce/SaaS/Restaurant), auto-categorize from your history, full keyboard shortcuts, bulk-select with undo, PWA shortcuts + Share Target, and a clear-sample-data button.

changes.text: Industry templates: pick Consulting, E-commerce, SaaS, Restaurant, or Generic on first run to get a tailored set of revenue + expense categories. Templates merge with existing categories — your data is never overwritten.

Auto-categorize from history: when you type a description that resembles a previous one, the app suggests the matching category with a one-tap 'Use this' button. Uses exact match, substring, then token overlap scoring.
Keyboard shortcuts: press ? anywhere to see the cheat sheet. n = new transaction, / = focus search, g+d/r/e/b/s/i/t/m = jump to view, Esc = close any dialog. Disabled while typing.
Bulk actions on Revenue and Expense: checkbox per row + select-all-on-page header. Floating action bar shows selection count; bulk delete uses the same 6-second Undo pattern as single deletes.
PWA shortcuts: long-press the app icon on Android/Chrome OS to see Add Transaction, Import CSV, and Dashboard quick actions.
Share Target API: 'Share to P&L Dashboard' now appears in your phone's share sheet for CSV and Excel files. Sharing routes to the import view ready for mapping.
Sample Data is now tagged so you can clear it in one click — the Dashboard shows a 'Clear Sample Data' button whenever demo transactions are loaded.

release_notes.title: Power Features — Undo, Search, Duplicates, Workers & Optimistic Sync
release_notes.summary: 5 high-impact upgrades adapted from Linear, Gmail, Stripe: undo any delete, instant search on Revenue/Expense, non-blocking CSV import via Web Worker, automatic duplicate detection on import, and live sync status indicators.

changes.text: Undo deletes: deleting a transaction now shows a 6-second 'Undo' toast (Linear/Gmail pattern) — no more confirm dialog, no more accidental data loss. The transaction is fully restored if you click Undo.
Instant inline search on Revenue and Expense tabs — search descriptions, categories, amounts, dates, and months all at once with 150ms debounce. Empty-state hint appears when no matches found.
Pagination Prev/Next controls now visible on Revenue and Expense tables — combined with search you can scan 100k+ rows without ever leaving the page.

Non-blocking CSV import via Web Worker: files over 500KB now parse on a background thread, so the UI stays responsive (typing, charts, scrolling) during big imports. Progress bar shows live parse progress.

Automatic duplicate detection on CSV import: rows matching existing transactions on date + amount + description + type are flagged. One-click choice to skip duplicates (recommended) or import everything.
Optimistic UI for Google Drive sync: top-bar status now shows 'Syncing to Google Drive…' then '✓ Synced' on every edit, removing the 'did it sync?' anxiety. Failures show 'Sync failed — will retry'.
CSP updated to allow blob: workers (required for the non-blocking CSV parsing) while keeping all other lock-down protections intact.

release_notes.title: CX Polish — Help, Install Prompt, Plain-Language Backup & Empty States
release_notes.summary: 7 usability improvements: smart CSV import with date/number format selectors, actionable empty states with sample data, in-app help drawer, smart PWA install banner, plain-English backup labels, and canonical URL.

changes.text: CSV import: date format selector (Auto-detect / US / European / ISO) and number format selector (Auto-detect / US 1,234.56 / EU 1.234,56) — no more silent parse failures on European bank exports
Empty state on Dashboard, Revenue, and Expense tabs: three CTA buttons (Add Transaction, Import CSV, Try Sample Data) guide first-time users instead of a blank screen
Sample Data mode: one click loads 6 months of realistic demo transactions so you can explore the app before entering real data
In-app Help drawer: ? button in the top bar opens a slide-in panel with Quick Start steps and 7 common-question FAQs with a link to the full User Guide
Smart PWA install banner: shows 'Install this app' only after you've added 3+ transactions (engaged users accept at ~25% vs ~3% on first load)
Backup tab labels renamed from developer jargon ('Layer 1/2/3') to plain English: Quick Save, Save to My Computer, Sync to Google Drive
Canonical URL meta tag added; manifest start_url updated to / so the app installs to the root URL

release_notes.title: License Key Sign-In + Blank-Page Hardening
release_notes.summary: Sign in to the app with just your email + license key — no Google account required. Plus defensive code so a corrupted cached session can never blank the screen.

changes.text: Alternative sign-in: use your email + license key (from your purchase receipt). No Google account needed to access the dashboard. Google sign-in remains the default; license-key entry is linked below the Google button.

Blank-page root cause fixed: an old or malformed cached session (missing user.plan or user.name) would throw an uncaught error in unlockApp() after the auth gate was hidden, leaving the screen blank. unlockApp() now handles every field defensively and restores the auth gate if anything goes wrong.
Boot flow wrapped in try/catch — if bootApp() itself crashes for any reason, the cached session is cleared and the auth gate is brought back so the user has a recoverable state.

Google Sheets sync is unchanged and remains optional — it's still accessed from Backup tab and uses Google OAuth separately from app sign-in. License-key users get full Sheets sync if they choose to enable it.

release_notes.title: Direct Index + CSP Fix for Google OAuth
release_notes.summary: Clean URL now serves the dashboard directly (no redirect dance) and Content-Security-Policy now allows Google OAuth iframes — fixes blank-page issue.

changes.text: Blank page at clean URL — index.html now contains the full dashboard directly instead of redirecting (eliminates redirect failure mode)
CSP frame-src 'none' was blocking Google OAuth iframes — relaxed to allow accounts.google.com
CSP also now allows Google profile images (lh3.googleusercontent.com) and oauth2.googleapis.com
Service worker pre-caches both index.html and pl-dashboard-v8.html so both URLs work offline

release_notes.title: Always-Latest Loader + One-Click Update
release_notes.summary: New clean URL with always-fresh loading, plus a 'Reload Now' button on the update banner that clears all caches and forces the latest build.

changes.text: Clean URL: https://apatel85.github.io/pl-dashboard/ — auto-redirects to the newest build with cache-busting query string
Update banner now has a 'Reload Now' button: clears service worker, drops all caches, and reloads to the latest version
Cache-Control headers on the HTML force browsers to revalidate on every visit
Service worker updated to v8.0.2 — old caches auto-purge on next load

release_notes.title: Mobile Layout Overhaul
release_notes.summary: Comprehensive mobile-first responsive redesign — proper stacking on phones, big tap targets, iOS safe-area support, full-screen modals on small screens, and bottom-pinned toasts.

changes.text: Charts now correctly stack vertically on mobile (was caused by a class name typo in mobile CSS)
All buttons and inputs meet 44px minimum tap-target size for accessibility
Form inputs use 16px font on mobile to prevent iOS auto-zoom on focus
iOS safe-area insets respected — no content hides behind notch or home indicator
Modals slide up from bottom on mobile (native app feel) instead of centered overlays
Mapping modal field grid stacks vertically on phones (was overlapping)
Backup tier rows wrap properly — status badges no longer overflow
Google Sheets connect card stacks on mobile so action buttons aren't cramped
Snapshot list rows wrap with action buttons on their own line on small screens
Sidebar drawer is now 85vw max width with proper iOS top padding
Toast position pinned to bottom-center on mobile, above iOS home indicator
PWA standalone mode hides the iOS install hint and adjusts top padding
Landscape orientation on small phones now scrolls modals properly

release_notes.title: Security, Performance & Offline Hardening
release_notes.summary: Audit-driven release: 19 security and reliability fixes, single self-contained file that works online AND offline, table pagination for 100k+ rows, and accessibility improvements.

changes.text: Single self-contained HTML — Chart.js + XLSX.js inlined, no CDN dependency. Works fully offline from a downloaded file.
XSS hardening — all user-controlled fields (descriptions, categories, CSV imports, toast messages) now properly HTML-escaped
Content-Security-Policy meta tag added — blocks injected scripts even if escaping is bypassed
CSV export now prefixes formula-injection cells (=, +, -, @) with a leading quote to prevent Excel formula execution
Revenue and Expense tables now paginate at 50 rows per page — instant render even with 100,000+ transactions
Snapshot quota errors now surface a clear toast instead of failing silently
Amount parser now handles accounting-negative format (99.00) and EU format 1.234,56
Date format selector in CSV mapping modal (auto / MM-DD-YYYY / DD-MM-YYYY)
CSV parser now correctly handles RFC 4180 escaped quotes and strips BOM
Monthly P&L total row now uses consistent Net Profit math (was mixing gross and net)
Double-confirmation for Clear All Data — two prompts before permanent deletion
User-facing error screen when IndexedDB is unavailable (private mode, quota exhausted)
Toast notifications now properly announce to screen readers (ARIA live region)
Float drift suppressed in displayed totals via Math.round(n*100)/100 in fmt()

release_notes.title: 3-Layer Backup + Google Sheets Cloud Sync
release_notes.summary: Full data protection with browser snapshots, auto-file backup, and Google Sheets live sync.

changes.text: Layer 1: Auto browser snapshots — last 5 states stored, one-click restore
Layer 2: Auto file backup every 30 min to your computer (Chrome/Edge/Brave)
Layer 3: Google Sheets live sync — push/pull cloud backup accessible from any device
Protection score banner showing which backup layers are active
In-app step-by-step Google sign-in guide — no technical knowledge needed
Persistent storage request — protects IndexedDB from browser eviction
Storage health dashboard with size estimates
All data changes trigger automatic snapshot scheduling

release_notes.title: IndexedDB Engine + File Sync
release_notes.summary: Complete data entry, IndexedDB storage for 100K+ rows, and local file sync.

changes.text: IndexedDB storage — handles 100,000+ transactions with proper indexing
Quick-Add form with Enter-key rapid entry
Inline editing of all transaction fields in the table
Paginated transactions table with sort, search, and multi-filter
File System Access API — sync directly to a CSV or XLSX on disk
Export to Excel (.xlsx) with Transactions + Monthly Summary sheets
Charts and dashboard fully async — no lag on large datasets

release_notes.title: Initial Release
release_notes.summary: Full-featured P&L dashboard with CSV import, charts, and auto-save.

changes.text: CSV upload with intelligent field mapping
Revenue & expense tracking with category breakdown
4 interactive charts: bar, line, and donut visualizations
Auto-save — data persists between sessions
Export to CSV and JSON backup/restore
